en_US.website_article: Two receiver labels on one HECTON-8 packet do not automatically prove a forged file. Public archives split the receiver problem into several lanes: the office named on the original address band, the relay node that first accepted the packet, the quarantine office that held it, the claimant desk that summarized it, and the legal archive that later filed it under a safer title. Those lanes can disagree without being harmless. The dangerous mistake is treating the cleanest label as the real one. Deep Reach paperwork often keeps the public-facing receiver narrow while moving the useful packet through a different custody path. Atlas recovery fragments show the same pattern in reverse: a relay receipt may look like ownership even when it only proves transit. The public archive therefore marks receiver conflict as ambiguity, not acquittal and not conviction.
en_US.wiki_article: Receiver ambiguity is a custody condition where a packet family contains more than one plausible receiving party. Common causes include relay lag, quarantine hold, claimant-safe rewriting, legal archive recategorization, and office-level shielding. The wiki may list the visible labels, but final receiver identity remains held until packet custody, witness hash, scanner gate, and terminal route evidence converge.
en_US.pda_codex: Archive note: receiver conflict found. Treat address band, relay receipt, quarantine hold, and claimant summary as separate facts. If the packet names a public office but the custody route points elsewhere, follow the physical route first. A clean receiver field can be a filing convenience. A dirty receiver field can be a delayed relay. Neither is enough alone.
en_US.scanner_entry: Receiver field mismatch. Address band and custody mark do not resolve to the same office. Confidence: partial. Required next evidence: relay timestamp, quarantine stamp, claimant-safe summary, or witness hash.
en_US.terminal_note: PUBLIC ARCHIVE RECEIVER AMBIGUITY Visible conflict: receiver label mismatch. Do not collapse address, relay, quarantine, claimant, and archive fields into one owner. Public summary may name the office allowed to answer. Custody route may show the office that actually held the packet. Action: hold final receiver text until route proof is present.
en_US.evidence_caption: Receiver ambiguity stamp. The packet has a public receiver label and a separate custody route. This proves conflict in paperwork, not final guilt, final innocence, rescue status, or ending consequence.
en_US.spoiler_policy: The phrase "receiver ambiguity" may appear early. The final receiver, route consequence, Atlas result, and legal result must remain masked until later proof gates. Public readers get the conflict category; players earn the route.
en_US.title: Public Archive Receiver Ambiguity

en_US.website_article: After HECTON-8, evidence did not move only through courts, archives, or rescue offices. It moved through cleanup bids. A cleanup bid is a paid request to sort a fragment into a safer category: damaged telemetry, claimant correspondence, obsolete repair notice, salvage lot attachment, insurance duplicate, or inadmissible route debris. The bid may be legal, predatory, desperate, or fraudulent. Its existence proves that someone wanted the record handled. The bid does not prove the record true. It does not prove it false. It does not prove the bidder caused the event. It shows pressure around the fragment and names the office willing to spend currency, favor, or leverage to change how the fragment travels. Deep Reach used cleanup bids as a public-safe shield. Marauder cells used the same market to recover trails before they were erased. Atlas-linked relays sometimes produced cleanup bids without knowing what the recovered packet meant.
en_US.wiki_article: Evidence cleanup bid: a market or administrative offer to clean, classify, relabel, suppress, or re-route a custody fragment. Related markers include payment hold, category rewrite, salvage lot recoding, claimant-safe summary request, and terminal redaction order. The wiki may list bid categories but must not name final buyer guilt, route outcome, or legal conclusion without later custody proof.

A bid can be placed by the guilty office, a frightened insurer, a claimant desk, a broker, a recovery crew, or a rival trying to buy the paper trail before Deep Reach does. Follow payment route, custody mark, and rewritten category.

en_US.website_article: A claimant-safe summary is not a neutral short version. It is a protected rewrite. It may remove names, collapse coordinates into a broad zone, replace injury detail with a category, turn a route action into a filing phrase, or replace a receiving office with an office allowed to answer public mail. Those edits can be necessary. They can also be exploited. HECTON-8 records make the difference visible because raw objects survive beside summary language. A scanner mark may show the real route while the summary says "transferred." A terminal may carry a pressure warning while the summary says "handled." A casualty detail may become "claimant risk." The conflict is not a lore error. It is a custody signal. The question is which omission protected a person and which omission protected an institution.
en_US.wiki_article: Claimant-safe summary conflict: a mismatch between protected public wording and object-level evidence. Common redactions include name removal, coordinate rounding, injury category replacement, office substitution, route softening, and legal status neutralization. The wiki may describe the conflict type, but protected details remain held until proof gates and spoiler policy permit them.
en_US.pda_codex: Codex warning: claimant-safe summary found. Do not assume the summary is false because it omits detail. Do not assume it is honest because it claims safety. Compare what it removes against the object: names, coordinates, injury specifics, receiver labels, route verbs, and payment lines.
en_US.scanner_entry: Claimant-safe summary conflict. Public wording does not match object route. Confidence: partial. Omitted fields: identity, coordinate, injury, receiver, or action verb. Required next proof: raw strip, witness hash, terminal stamp, or custody transfer.
en_US.terminal_note: CLAIMANT-SAFE SUMMARY CONFLICT Summary text is safe for public handling. Raw object may not be safe. Do not restore protected names or coordinates from guesswork. Action: preserve omission list, route proof, and claimant risk marker.
en_US.evidence_caption: Claimant-safe summary strip. The omission itself is evidence. It may protect a claimant, protect an office, or protect a payment route. It does not resolve final truth.
